MOLECULAR ONCOLOGY REPORT
[redacted name] Cancer Center
Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Diagnosis: Non-small cell lung cancer, possible large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
Specimen Type: Right lung biopsy
Estimated Tumor Content: 20%

TEST PERFORMED
Comprehensive Solid Tumor Panel - DNA and RNA Analysis

METHODOLOGY
DNA Analysis: Targeted next-generation sequencing of hotspot regions and full coding sequences across 45 cancer-related genes using molecular barcoded primers and amplicon-based library preparation. Sequencing performed on integrated platform with 5% variant allele frequency (VAF) detection limit.

RNA Analysis: Targeted RNA sequencing for detection of gene fusions and splice variants in 17 kinase genes using molecular barcoded primers.

Sample Processing: Automated nucleic acid extraction and purification from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue.

Quality Requirements: Minimum 100× coverage depth required for variant calling.

QUALITY ASSESSMENT
DNA Quality: FAILED - Insufficient amplicon coverage across target regions
RNA Quality: FAILED - RNA degradation below acceptable threshold
Tumor Content: 20% (minimum 20% recommended)

TEST RESULTS

DNA PANEL ANALYSIS: FAILED
Genes Attempted: EGFR, KRAS, BRAF, ALK, ROS1, RET, MET, NTRK1/2/3, and 35 additional genes
Result: Unable to complete analysis due to reduced amplicon coverage. Variant detection for activating mutations, resistance mutations, and other clinically relevant alterations could not be performed.

RNA PANEL ANALYSIS: FAILED
Fusions/Splice Variants Attempted: ALK fusions, ROS1 fusions, RET fusions, MET exon 14 skipping, NTRK1/2/3 fusions, and 12 additional fusion targets
Result: Unable to complete analysis due to insufficient RNA quality. Fusion detection and splice variant analysis could not be performed.

ACTIONABLE FINDINGS
None identified - test failure

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
The failed analysis prevents determination of eligibility for the following FDA-approved targeted therapies:
- EGFR inhibitors (erlotinib, gefitinib, afatinib, osimertinib, dacomitinib)
- ALK inhibitors (crizotinib, ceritinib, alectinib, brigatinib, lorlatinib)
- ROS1 inhibitors (crizotinib, entrectinib)
- BRAF/MEK inhibitors (dabrafenib/trametinib)
- RET inhibitors (selpercatinib, pralsetinib)
- MET inhibitors (capmatinib, tepotinib)
- NTRK inhibitors (larotrectinib, entrectinib)
- KRAS G12C inhibitors (sotorasib, adagrasib)

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Consider repeat testing using material from a separate specimen if clinically indicated
2. Alternative specimen with higher tumor content (>30%) may improve test success rate
3. Fresh frozen tissue or cytology specimens may provide better nucleic acid quality
4. If repeat molecular testing is not feasible, consider immunohistochemistry for ALK and ROS1 as alternative screening methods

TEST LIMITATIONS
- This assay requires minimum tumor content of 20% and adequate nucleic acid quality
- Detection limit is 5% VAF for single nucleotide variants and small insertions/deletions
- Large genomic rearrangements outside targeted regions will not be detected
- RNA degradation in FFPE specimens may limit fusion detection sensitivity

Electronically signed by: Dr. [redacted name], MD, PhD
Board Certified in Molecular Genetic Pathology
